title: The Group Chat of Cedar Falls
premise: Mirabel Thornbury, the meticulous statistician for Cedar Falls High's championship team, has spent five years keeping his head down and his numbers clean — until he discovers his late grandmother's recipe box hides coded instructions exposing a decades-long scheme by the school board to rig athletic eligibility, funding, and futures. With the help of his found family — the team's disgraced ex-captain, a whistleblower janitor, and the board chair's daughter he's falling for — Mirabel decodes the archive before the board can destroy it and pin the leak on him. In the end, Mirabel chooses truth over safety at devastating personal cost, but the family he built along the way refuses to let him pay it alone.
about_author: Sebastian Ishikawa is a former small-town sports statistician who writes young adult fiction about the quiet kids who notice everything. He lives in the Pacific Northwest with two cats and an unhealthy collection of index cards.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. During the state semifinal, Mirabel notices statistical anomalies in player eligibility records that shouldn't exist. He buries the observation, as he always does, and goes home to sort his grandmother's belongings after her funeral. Emotional beat: the ache of being careful for so long that silence feels like identity.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Cipher
chapters.summary: Still Mirabel's POV. Cleaning out grandma's kitchen, he finds her recipe box — and tucked behind the cardamom cake recipe, a hand-drawn cipher keyed to school board meeting minutes from 1998. The first decoded line reads: 'They know I know.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Five Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Mirabel's POV, revealing why he learned to be invisible: a middle-school incident where telling the truth got another kid expelled. Establishes his found family — teammates Dez and Priya, who drag him out of isolation. Emotional beat: tenderness disguised as annoyance.

chapters.title: The Janitor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Earl, the night custodian, who once saw grandma Thornbury photographing board documents. When Mirabel asks him oblique questions, Earl warns him: 'The last person who asked got a scholarship they never earned — and a debt they did.' Emotional beat: fear passing like a baton.

chapters.title: Recipe for Ruin
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Decoding further, he learns the 'scholarship pipeline' funnels star athletes through falsified residency papers, and when they burn out, their records vanish. One vanished name is Dez's older brother. Emotional beat: guilt — Mirabel's clean numbers helped hide dirty hands.

chapters.title: Dessert First
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez confronts Mirabel about his distraction, and Mirabel almost tells him everything — then doesn't. Instead he tests the waters by asking about Dez's brother, and watches Dez shut down completely. Emotional beat: the loneliness of protection.

chapters.title: The Chair's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV of Wren Calloway, the board chair's daughter and Mirabel's lab partner, who catches him photographing board minutes in the library. Instead of reporting him, she admits she's found her father's burner phone. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: attraction tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A decoded map leads to a storage unit holding grandma's real archive: twenty years of ledgers, recordings, and a list of 'debts' — students traded like currency. The final page is addressed to Mirabel by name. Emotional beat: being seen by someone who's gone.

chapters.title: Eligibility
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers her own athletic scholarship was manufactured to keep her compliant, and her father knows she's been asking questions. First real fight between Wren and Mirabel about whether to go public or go slow. Emotional beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Homecoming week; the town celebrates the team while Priya notices board members quietly shredding in the admin office after hours. She photographs them and joins the group without being asked. Emotional beat: courage arriving sideways, through loyalty.

chapters.title: The Group Chat
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter told through the five friends' encrypted group chat messages. They name themselves 'The Recipe Box' and divide the archive: Mirabel decodes, Wren handles her father, Earl provides access, Dez and Priya gather testimony. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Earl's POV. Earl is fired on fabricated grounds — a warning shot aimed at whoever's been snooping. He gives Mirabel a key and one instruction: 'Finish her recipe.' Emotional beat: sacrifice without drama, the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The board announces an 'archive modernization' — the physical records will be destroyed Friday. Mirabel realizes grandma anticipated this: the cipher's final layer requires a document only accessible inside the board office. Emotional beat: the trap tightening around hope.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts her father privately; he offers her everything — protection, the scholarship made honest, Mirabel's safety — if she hands over the archive. She says she needs time. Emotional beat: duty wearing the mask of love.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Split POV between Mirabel and Dez during the break-in at the board office. They retrieve the master ledger, but trip a silent alarm. Dez covers Mirabel's escape and is caught. Emotional beat: terror, then the sick math of who pays.

chapters.title: Collateral
chapters.summary: Dez's POV, from a juvenile detention hold. The board frames Dez for theft and vandalism, threatening expulsion and charges — exactly what happened to his brother. Mirabel, watching from outside, understands: this is the debt system working as designed. Emotional beat: rage with nowhere to go.

chapters.title: Grandma's Last Ingredient
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The final cipher layer reveals grandma's masterstroke: duplicate archives already mailed to journalists, lawyers, and the state athletics commission — sealed, released only if she died unnaturally or the archive was destroyed. But the trigger requires verification only Mirabel can provide. Emotional beat: inheritance as responsibility.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation across the day of destruction. The friends execute a desperate plan: verify the dead-man's switch, stall the shredding, and get Wren's testimony on record. Wren chooses Mirabel over her father, live-recording his confession attempt. Emotional beat: every choice arriving at once.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the emergency board meeting, Mirabel stands before the town that taught him to be quiet and presents the numbers — his language, finally weaponized. The state investigators arrive mid-meeting with the verified archive. Emotional beat: the careful boy speaking anyway.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fallout: resignations, criminal referrals, Dez freed and his brother's record posthumously cleared. But Wren loses her father entirely, and the town turns on the kids who exposed its pride. Emotional beat: victory that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: What We Kept
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Weeks later, the group gathers in grandma's emptied kitchen. Mirabel confesses how long he stayed silent and why; instead of judgment, they give him the thing he never had — permission to be imperfect. He and Wren finally name what they are to each other. Emotional beat: grace.

chapters.title: New Season
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Mirabel's POV, epilogue-style. Spring tryouts under new oversight; Mirabel publishes an independent audit column in the school paper titled 'The Numbers Don't Lie.' The recipe box sits on his desk, empty except for one blank card he's started writing on. Emotional beat: power reclaimed as care.
